turns.assessment: The approximately 4.4 dB drop is already present at the input of the S06→S19 booster and then propagates through every amplifier and multiple monitored channels. Stable pump currents rule against amplifier failure, while a span fault after the booster could not lower the booster input. A partially lossy OMS input connector at S06, plausibly associated with the recent S06 maintenance, best matches the persistent all-channel power reduction; a pulled connector or WSS port failure would instead cause signal loss.

proposals.rationale: Contamination on the patch between the S06 ROADM degree and the S06→S19 booster would reduce all channels before amp0, explaining the equal input/output reductions across all seven amplifiers and the downstream OCM channel-power drops. The unchanged pump currents and recent maintenance at S06 support this diagnosis.
